title: Why do we have seasons?
examples: Does the Earth get closer to the Sun in summer?
If the Earth is tilted, does that change the seasons?
Why are some places sunny and others cold at the same time?

explain.say: The Earth is actually tilted a little bit as it goes around the Sun.
This tilt means that different parts of Earth get more sunlight at different times.
The tilt causes different hemispheres to receive direct sunlight at different times.
When your part of Earth is tilted towards the Sun, you get more sunlight.
For example, when the Northern Hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun, it is summer there.
In real life, this tilt helps us know when to plant our best crops.

faq.q: Does the distance from the Sun change the seasons?
faq.a: No, the distance from the Sun does not cause the seasons. The tilt of the Earth is the main reason.
asks: Is it because we are closer to the Sun?
Does the orbit distance matter for seasons?

faq.q: Why do some places have summer while others have winter?
faq.a: It is because the Earth's tilt means different hemispheres get more direct sunlight at different times.
asks: How can two places have different weather at once?
Does the tilt cause different seasons?

faq.a: A hemisphere is half of the Earth. The Earth is divided into two halves by the equator.
asks: What are the two halves of Earth?
Can you name the two hemispheres?

faq.q: Does the Earth stop tilting at any point?
faq.a: No, the Earth maintains its tilt as it revolves around the Sun throughout its orbit.
asks: Does the tilt change over time?

faq.q: If the Earth was not tilted, would we still have seasons?
faq.a: No, without the tilt, all parts of Earth would get the same amount of sunlight all the time.
asks: What if the Earth was straight?

facts: The Earth is tilted on its axis as it orbits the Sun.
The tilt causes different hemispheres to receive varying amounts of sunlight.
The seasons are caused by the tilt, not by the distance from the Sun.
The Earth takes one year to complete one full orbit around the Sun.

quiz.say: The main reason for Earth's seasons is:

options.show: The tilt of the Earth's axis
options.say: The tilt of the Earth's axis

options.show: Getting closer to the Sun in summer
options.say: Getting closer to the Sun in summer

quiz.why: The tilt causes different parts of Earth to receive varying amounts of sunlight throughout the year.

wrong.0: This is incorrect because the Moon affects tides, not the yearly seasons.
wrong.1: The Sun's energy output is steady, not changing to cause seasons.
wrong.3: This is a common mistake because people think distance causes temperature changes.

quiz.say: When one hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun, it experiences:
quiz.why: Tilting towards the Sun means the sunlight hits that area more directly and strongly.

wrong.0: Moonlight is much weaker than direct sunlight from the Sun.
wrong.1: The tilt ensures the intensity of light changes seasonally.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the tilt ensures some parts get extra light.

quiz.say: If the Earth had no tilt, what would happen to the seasons?

options.show: All regions would get similar sunlight year-round
options.say: All regions would get similar sunlight year-round

options.show: It would be always winter everywhere
options.say: It would be always winter everywhere

quiz.why: Without the tilt, the sunlight would hit all parts of Earth more evenly, eliminating seasons.

wrong.0: The Sun's energy source is not related to the Earth's tilt.
wrong.1: Orbital speed is not directly controlled by the tilt.
wrong.3: This is too extreme; some light would still reach the Earth.
